body:
## Why

**Observed 2026-09-03: a healthy dispatcher took itself down over a worker's commit and the board went
silent for six hours.**

`.kanban/logs/dispatch.log`:

```
2026-09-03T16:50:28.601Z tick: reconciled 0 reclaimed 0 ... claimed 0 ...
2026-09-03T16:50:28.615Z FATAL hkb: this loop is running 238a3b65d997, the installed hkb is
                         b9aef19f1a87 — restarting. Running workers are untouched.
```

- `238a3b6` is the checkout's HEAD, and it never moved: `git log --oneline -1` in the repo root still
  reports it, and `git status` is clean.
- `b9aef19` is **a commit on `worktree-kb-334-1`** — the branch of the worker that was running at the
  time. It is not on `main`, was never merged, and is not what the dispatcher is executing.

So the self-heal ladder — which exists to restart a loop whose code is genuinely stale (#140) — compared
the loop against a *worker's worktree* and gave itself up. `hkb up` is deliberately not a supervisor, so
nothing restarted it. Cards sat in `ready` from 16:50 to 22:37 with a serve process up, a pid file
present, and every card looking normal on the web board. The operator noticed from the board being still,
not from any signal hkb produced.

**Why this is worse than a stalled loop.** The failure is silent and self-inflicted, and the state it
leaves is indistinguishable from an idle board: `hkb up --status` says `dispatch exited (4)`, but nothing
watches that, and `hkb watch` — the documented monitor — reports *board transitions*, of which a dead
dispatcher produces exactly none. A guard that stops all work when it misfires needs to be much harder to
misfire than this one is.

## What

1. **Find out what `installStamp()` is actually reading.** It is documented as "the checkout's own
   `git rev-parse HEAD` when it has one, the package version otherwise, both read fresh off disk"
   (`docs/wiki/architecture/overview.md`). It returned a commit that exists only on a linked worktree's
   branch, so either the `git rev-parse` runs with a cwd that can land in a worktree, or it resolves the
   *installed* `hkb` (a global npm link) to a path that is not the loop's own checkout. Both are plausible
   here: this machine has had an `hkb` npm-link drift before, and hkb creates linked worktrees constantly.
   Reproduce it before fixing it.
2. **Pin the comparison to the loop's own module path**, not to a cwd and not to whatever `hkb` resolves
   to on `PATH`. The question the guard asks is "has the code *this process imported* been replaced", so
   the answer must come from the directory that process's entry point lives in
   (`fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`), resolved through `--git-dir`/`--git-common-dir` so a linked
   worktree answers with the common repository rather than its own branch tip.
3. **A stamp mismatch must be corroborated before it is fatal.** Exit 4 stops all work; it should require
   more than one unequal string. At minimum, confirm the new sha is an ancestor-or-equal of the checkout's
   HEAD, or that the entry file's mtime actually changed — a commit that is on neither is a bug in the
   probe, not a redeploy, and should log loudly and keep ticking.
4. **Say it where someone will see it.** `hkb watch` streams board transitions and a dead dispatcher makes
   none, so the one monitor the operate procedure prescribes cannot report this. Either `hkb watch` emits a
   `dispatcher` event when the loop it is watching goes away, or the exit-4 line becomes something
   `hkb doctor` reports as a hard `✗` with the restart command — silence is the actual defect here.

## Done when

- [ ] The misfire is reproduced in a test: a loop in a checkout that has linked worktrees, whose branches
      carry commits the checkout's HEAD does not, keeps running.
- [ ] A genuine redeploy (HEAD of the loop's own checkout really moves) still exits 4 — that behaviour is
      correct and must not be lost.
- [ ] An uncorroborated mismatch logs and continues rather than exiting.
- [ ] A dead dispatcher is visible to something the operator is already looking at.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` green.

## Contract

Do not remove the self-heal ladder — #140 is real, and a loop running code that a merge replaced is a
genuine hazard. This narrows *what counts as evidence* that it happened. Errors name the fix and carry
`.exitCode`; `--json` everywhere.
title: installStamp compared the loop against a worker's worktree commit and killed a healthy dispatcher for six hours
